title: SharePoint: campaigns in SharePoint sites for organising, distributing and measuring news
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's licensing statements, rollout windows and exclusion of site campaigns from the Amplify campaign-creation setting. Narrow the absolute claim about autonomous behaviour to what Microsoft describes, and preserve the expected rather than guaranteed rollout completion date.

claims.claim: Site campaigns bring Viva Amplify campaign management into SharePoint sites in a lighter-weight form.
claims.quote: This is a complementary way to create lighter weight campaigns inside a SharePoint site as a way to organize your SharePoint news posts

claims.claim: Users can organise related SharePoint news posts into site campaigns.
claims.quote: Site campaigns can be used to organize related SharePoint news posts

claims.claim: Site campaigns can publish news posts across SharePoint.
claims.quote: publish these news posts across SharePoint, Viva Engage, Teams and Outlook Email.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe site campaigns at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: '"site campaigns" "SharePoint"'; '"campaigns in SharePoint" permissions analytics audience targeting licensing seeded'. Opened Viva Amplify setup and access-policy pages; results describe other SharePoint experiences or Amplify app campaigns, not site campaigns.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and .api; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No admin UI, feature access policy or automation for enabling site campaigns or restricting their creators is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"site campaigns" admin settings PowerShell Graph Viva feature access policy'; 'SharePoint site campaigns Set-SPOTenant Set-SPOSite Microsoft Graph campaign creation disable'; 'Set-SPOTenant "Campaign" parameter'. Opened Amplify setup, manage-access-policies and Set-SPOTenant syntax.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Roles; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the site role or permission required to create a site campaign.
claims.quote: Searched: '"campaigns in SharePoint" permissions analytics audience targeting licensing seeded'; 'SharePoint "site campaigns" analytics metrics audience permissions'. Read Amplify setup and roles excerpts; those describe Amplify app roles, not site campaign creation permissions.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how site campaign publishing applies audience targeting or site permissions across channels.
claims.quote: Searched: '"campaigns in SharePoint" permissions analytics audience targeting licensing seeded'; 'SharePoint "site campaigns" analytics metrics audience permissions'. Read audience-targeting excerpts for SharePoint app in Teams and Amplify setup; neither describes site campaign cross-channel enforcement.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described site campaign analytics metrics or their level of detail.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint "site campaigns" analytics metrics audience permissions'; '"campaigns in SharePoint" permissions analytics audience targeting licensing seeded'. Read Amplify setup and SharePoint app for Teams analytics excerpts; they describe neighbouring experiences, not site campaign metrics.

claims.claim: The supplied notice describes no new identity, sign-in or permission model.
claims.quote: A new SharePoint experience will allow users to create lightweight site campaigns directly within SharePoint.

claims.claim: The feature does not act on its own: a person has to create a campaign and publish.
claims.quote: Searched: '"site campaigns" "SharePoint"'; '"campaigns in SharePoint" permissions analytics audience targeting licensing seeded'. Read MC1568699 and Amplify setup; they describe user capabilities but do not state that every action requires a person or exclude autonomous behaviour categorically.
claims.fix: Replace 'The feature does not act on its own: a person has to create a campaign and publish.' with 'MC1568699 describes users creating site campaigns and publishing news posts; it describes no autonomous behaviour.'

claims.claim: Microsoft's supplied descriptions concern people creating and publishing campaigns and describe no autonomous behaviour.
claims.quote: A new SharePoint experience will allow users to create lightweight site campaigns directly within SharePoint. ... Site campaigns can be used to organize related SharePoint news posts, and publish these news posts
